# Global Trendes

Sourced November–December 2026 travel atlas. Snapshot: 2026-11-02.

- Atlas: data/atlas.json — 250 country/territory records, researched events, holiday calendars, historical markets, archived annual statistics, seasonal notes and source URLs.
- Country coverage: data/coverage.json — counts and observation periods for every country/territory.
- Primary research: data/curated-research.json — expanded events, direction-specific markets, historical monthly observations and exclusions.
- Archived indicators: data/travel-statistics.json — World Bank/UN Tourism annual arrivals, departures, receipts and expenditure, generally stopping in 2020; units and years explicit.
- Background source index: data/sources.json — retrieved pages with URLs, timestamps, metadata and content hashes. Exact totals: data/crawl-stats.json; failed/skipped requests: data/crawl-failures.json.
- Seasonal sources: data/seasonal-research.json.

## Calendar

The calendar supports country, continent and worldwide scopes, entry-type filtering and date agendas. Prefer event.dates arrays over the outer start/end range: selected-day events are not continuously open. Null exact dates remain off the day grid. dateStatus and scheduleNote identify confirmed programmes, fixed annual dates, tentative calendars and previous-edition watchlists. All selected months are in 2026. Local events are not exhaustive, and a holiday is not proof of tourism demand.

## Inbound travel and outbound travel

travel[code].directions.inbound/outbound retain markets, period, label, note, metrics and a direction-specific URL. Some records also contain monthly['11'/'12'] actual historical November/December 2024 evidence; never relabel this as 2026. Other profiles retain annual or other historical monthly periods. Eurostat inbound accommodation arrivals differ from outbound resident overnight trips. Lists of separately reported countries are not exhaustive worldwide rankings. Mauritius outbound disembarkation can include transit points.

travelStats[code] is a SEPARATE archived annual World Bank/UN Tourism series, generally through 2020 and sometimes older. The pandemic affects 2020; 2019 is a separate reference. These totals are not bilateral rankings, unique people, forecasts or measured November/December 2026 demand. Empty/null means missing evidence, not zero travel. Cancelled/postponed programmes are excluded. The site does not automatically refresh research.

The wider automated source corpus is general background, not all month-specific or manually verified claims. Distinct host counts include subdomains rather than registrable domains. A source associated with a country can discuss related places; inspect its scope.

## Browser

Query: ?country=AE&month=11&tab=events&continent=Asia
Country ISO alpha-2; month 11 or12; tab events/inbound/outbound/guide; continent Africa,Asia,Europe,North America,South America,Oceania,Antarctic,or all. The directory includes small islands missing from polygons. Calendar scope has its own labelled control. JSON country briefs include dated/undated events, holidays, historical markets, archived statistics and limitations.

Local browser helpers: window.globalTrendes.getSelection(), selectCountry('AE'), setMonth(12), exportBrief(). No user data is transmitted.

## Detailed country rankings and city guides

Default travel view shows up to20 leading reported positions, including tied observations at rank20. Full-list search preserves original ranks; it never promotes an outside-top20 market into a fabricated rank. India uses annual2025 country annexes in the government’s India Tourism Statistics2026 (data/india-research.json):220 outbound and215 inbound individually reported markets. USoutbound#4, Vietnam#13, HongKong#22. Indian national departures count movements across all travel purposes, including repeats; they are not unique holidaymakers. Purpose shares and derived leisure estimates have their own labels and source pages.

The measurement selector separates a latest researched country table from historical same-month evidence where available. Greenland has33named annual2025 cruise residence markets and12named foreign accommodation-night markets; these are different populations and units. Its19rankedtowns/ports count cruise passenger visits, including repeats across ports. Outbound resident destination ranks were not verified and must not be inferred from air-passenger residence or routes. Full Greenland research: data/greenland-research.json.

Expanded country rows include source-table links, counts, available purpose shares and official destination city/town guides. These guides are editorial examples, not measured city ranks for travellers from a selected origin. HongKong and Singapore neighbourhoods/islands must not be relabelled as separate cities. Measured Greenland port ranks remain separately labelled. Source tables with fewer than20 named observations are shown at their actual length; no padding with invented destinations.

Attribution: Wikivoyage/Wikipedia linked contributors CC BY-SA4.0; Natural Earth public domain; mledoze/countries ODbL; date-holidays ISC; World Bank/UN Tourism CC BY4.0; Eurostat EC reuse policy; Unsplash License. Regional mood images need not depict the event or selected country. Reference boundaries imply no sovereignty position.

Global detail update (2Nov2026):69 numeric inbound country/territory profiles,38 numeric outbound profiles,65 inbound and20 outbound sources with20+ markets. Cityguides cover94 destinations and399 places. coverage.json includes numeric row and city counts. Country directory filters detail/continent and opens direction-specific briefs. Map arcs follow the visible/search-selected market list.
Metrics may use valueType=percentage and precision; format as percentages, never as arrival counts. US SIAT2025 overseas-air destination shares exclude Canada/Mexico and are not all-US outbound counts. UAE2024 publishes only five rounded source-market shares. GB ONS tables are GreatBritain, excludingNorthernIreland. ASEAN compilation/national source scope, Brunei air-only, HongKongJan–Feb2026 and Nepal earlier/revised2025 totals remain explicitly separated. Source rows may be grouped where the publisher reports a combined market; do not split or assign them to one country.

All-place update2November2026: all250 records have reviewed place guidance or local-scope sources. destinationGuides contains246 guides and1,433 places; sourceType=community identifies152 Wikivoyage adaptations with licence, attribution, revision/hash and retrieval metadata. Do not describe these as official tourism-board guides or measured city ranks. Four local-scope exceptions are not fabricated city lists.

travelReferences[code].inbound/outbound provides selected leading2019 source observations. historicalReference=true is mandatory; outbound mirrored=true refers ONLY to a62-destination reporting sample of border-tourist arrivals by usual residence. These are not current demand, departure surveys or complete worldwide destination ranks. Current numeric travel[code].directions records take priority; fallback uses dated references. Inbound reference definitions differ per reporter and must be preserved.

relatedEvidence[code].inbound/outbound stores index pointers {reporterCode,reporterDirection,metricIndex} into current travel direction metrics. These reverse-direction observations are an unranked evidence index; their years, units and populations differ and must never be pooled into a numeric Top20. Country brief exports resolve the full source records. placeApplicability explains statistical/jurisdictional exceptions; never inherit a parent-country total or assume a small population means zero tourism.

Primary numeric profiles:81 inbound/43 outbound. Historical references:181 inbound/236 outward reporting-sample views. Preferred current/reference coverage:185 inbound/236 outbound.20+ retained records:147 inbound/100 outbound. Complete current global Top20 ranks for every place are NOT claimed.
